name: Types of SAE Programs

objectives.text: Describe a Supervised Agricultural Experience as a hands-on project where students learn about agriculture by doing real work outside the classroom
Give examples of hands-on agricultural projects young people carry out, such as raising livestock, growing a garden, or working on a farm
Distinguish between a Foundational SAE and an Immersion SAE
List the five components of a Foundational SAE: career exploration and planning, employability skills, personal financial management, workplace safety, and agricultural literacy
Describe the Immersion SAE types of entrepreneurship, placement or internship, research, school-based enterprise, and service-learning
Explain how completing a Foundational SAE prepares a student to begin an Immersion SAE
Define SAE as work-based learning and explain its place alongside classroom instruction and FFA in the three-component model of agricultural education
Categorize sample student projects as foundational or immersion and by specific immersion type
Compare the components of foundational and immersion SAEs and explain the relationship between the two
Distinguish among experimental, analytical, and invention research SAEs using examples from agricultural science
Compare entrepreneurship and placement SAEs in terms of ownership, financial risk, compensation, and decision-making responsibility
Explain how school-based enterprise and service-learning SAEs differ from individually owned or employer-based projects
Analyze the lifelong learning and career skills developed through each type of SAE
Analyze which SAE type best fits a given student's interests, resources, and location
Explain how different SAE types connect to FFA proficiency award areas and FFA degree requirements
Explain how an SAE can grow or change type over time, such as a placement developing into an entrepreneurship
Evaluate the impact different SAE types have on student learning and future career readiness
Justify the selection of an SAE type based on career goals, available resources, and community needs

changes: Kept and reworded the definition, foundational versus immersion, immersion type comparison, fit analysis, and justification objectives. Dropped the grade 11 project planning objective because planning belongs to the Planning & Setting SAE Goals sibling. Added the five Foundational SAE components, school-based enterprise as an immersion type, research subtypes, entrepreneurship versus placement comparison, categorizing projects, the three-component model, skills developed by type, links to FFA proficiencies and degrees, how SAEs evolve between types, and evaluating the learning value of types. Mapped AFNR FPS codes to grade 9 to 12 objectives only.
